slides.title: What is a Standard ?
slides.body:
Networking Basics
A standard is a set of specifications/agreements adopted to ensure that hardware, software, and protocols work together globally

slides.title: Why Standards Are Needed ?
slides.body:
Networking Basics
To ensure devices and software from different companies can communicate smoothly
To ensure reliable and predictable communication
To allow global compatibility and network scalability
To provide common rules for protocols and network operations

slides.title: Examples of Standards
slides.body:
Networking Basics
IEEE / ISO standards ensure all devices follow the same rules so they can work together easily
Example: Wi-Fi routers from different brands can connect to any laptop or phone because they follow the same Wi-Fi standard

slides.title: IP Address
slides.body:
IP Address
1. Public IP Address
This IP address is globally unique and can be routed over the internet
Public IP addresses are used for websites, servers, and other resources available to the general public
A Public IP address is assigned to devices that are directly accessible over the internet
Example: Google IP address 142.250.72.46

slides.title: IP Address
slides.body:
IP Address
2. Private IP Address
A Private IP address is used within a local network and is not routable over the internet
Example: IP address ranging from 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255 
These addresses are used for devices that need to communicate with each other within a local network, such as in homes or offices
